source.independentAudit: Recomputed original ZIP byte SHA256 against Actions upload hash, verified all 15 entries and all four source-vectors, original client samples, every independently recorded PostgreSQL transaction COMMIT timestamp, 60-bin histograms, source hot-skew distributions by phase, per-transfer ledger effects (2 postings + 1 outbox), 28/28 SQL oracle outputs, and the exact 12 warmup-only missed offers in 320/direct. All original trial observations match their per-trial JSON. State SHA parity required only when both routes durably executed identical offers.

historicalC01.description: The earlier all-secondary C01 grain-placement precondition failure remains unexplained, though separate PR #47 added fail-closed diagnostics and a later C01 case passed.

interpretation.es: Se ofrecieron 59.520 transferencias sintéticas en cuatro ensayos de 62 segundos, con 60 segundos de medición por ensayo. PostgreSQL confirma 59.508 COMMIT persistidos, 119.016 asientos y 59.508 eventos outbox, con 28/28 oráculos SQL correctos. Las tasas observadas dentro de las ventanas fueron 160,0 y 320,0 COMMIT/s tanto para el acceso directo como para Orleans. Las 12 solicitudes no admitidas aparecieron exclusivamente al inicio del calentamiento de la ruta directa a 320/s (entre los segundos 0,100 y 0,134) por el límite de 32 operaciones simultáneas; ninguna pertenecía a la ventana de medición y ninguna tuvo efecto contable. A 320/s el estado SQL final difiere entre rutas porque una ruta no ejecutó esas 12 solicitudes iniciales; no es una discrepancia inexplicada de PostgreSQL. A 320/s en Orleans el recuento de COMMIT por segundo varía entre 319 y 321. Una repetición y un host físico NO demuestran saturación, p99 de producción ni equivalencia con un mainframe. Los percentiles calculados solo sobre confirmaciones están sesgados cuando se excluyen solicitudes perdidas.
interpretation.en: Four 62-second trials offered 59,520 synthetic transfer intents, each with a 60-second measurement window. PostgreSQL independently confirms 59,508 durable COMMIT operations, 119,016 postings, 59,508 outbox events and 28/28 passing independent SQL Oracle Gates. Measured in-window server COMMIT rates were 160.0 and 320.0 per second for both direct and Orleans routes. Exactly 12 offered intents were not admitted during the beginning of the 320/s direct-route warmup (at 0.100-0.134s) because of the 32 in-flight client limit; none belonged to the measurement window and none created ledger effects. The different final SQL state for 320/s direct and Orleans is fully explained by the 12 undispached warmup intents. At 320/s the Orleans per-second SQL COMMIT bins vary from 319 to 321. One repetition on one physical host does NOT prove a saturation knee, production p99 or mainframe MIPS equivalence. ACK-only latency percentiles are survivor-biased when missed offers are excluded.

limitations: One physical GitHub Linux runner with four disposable Podman namespaces, 1s warmup + 60s measurement + 1s cooldown, only one hot-source profile and one trial per rate/route. 32 in-flight admission cap can cause client-side loss distinct from SQL saturation. No 3+ independent runner cohorts, no physical multi-host HA, no isolated generator host, no comprehensive SQL pool/wait/CPU/GC/network sampling or fixed production SLO. SQL transfer COMMIT timestamps from PostgreSQL do not measure mainframe IBM Z MIPS. At 320/s one route's final SQL SHA differs due to 12 recorded never-dispatched warmup offers; this is not a hidden ledger inconsistency. E2 remains partially_verified, issues #8/#24/#25/#44 OPEN, C04 #34 UNVERIFIED, release v2026.10.29 unchanged.
